alex: Heads up — ran an apples-to-apples streaming vs non-streaming replay with the new kernel-selection change and saw a tail regression on streaming.

alex: p50 ~ 35ms (same), p95 went from ~42ms -> 140ms, p99 jumped to ~320ms after the kernel switchover point. Happens at chunk boundary when sequence length crosses 1024.

maria: ugh. did KV cache hit-rate change? or was that a pure kernel fallback?

alex: quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:01Z] request=xyz selected_kernel=attn_fused_fast seq_len=960
[2026-03-17T10:12:01Z] request=xyz selected_kernel=attn_fused_fast seq_len=1016
[2026-03-17T10:12:02Z] request=xyz kernel_fallback=attn_generic_slow reason="exceeds_fast_seq_threshold"
[2026-03-17T10:12:02Z] request=xyz latency_tokens_ms=210
```
Looks like when a chunk crosses that threshold we fall back to the generic path and latency spikes. But only in streaming mode the backlog/queueing amplifies it.

tj: that's consistent with batching heuristics — if one request hits slow kernel, it can hold the dispatch queue and cause backpressure. What are your batching params? max_batch_wait_ms / max_batch_size?

alex: current bench cfg (streaming): `max_batch_wait_ms=25`, `max_batch_size=32`, `chunk_size=256`. Using replay harness v3 (which replays the client-side read timings). Synthetic load (synth-driver) pre-warms cache and sends slightly different inter-chunk timing; synth didn't show the same p99.

sam: important — our replay harness v3 uses recorded client pacing, but our synthetic load fires more uniformly which lets KV cache stay hot. I ran a quick stats dump: KV_CACHE_HIT under replay = 0.74, synth = 0.97 for these traces. So cache churn + kernel fallback = multiplier effect.

perf-bot: regression-detect: commit=fa3b2c1 kernel-selector:increase-fast-threshold triggered_alert=tail-latency-streaming p99+35% vs baseline

maria: plan: we need apples-to-apples test that replays both client pacing and cold/warm cache states. Also capture kernel-selection markers and per-dispatch queue depth. Can we add perf markers: `KERNEL_SWITCH`, `BATCH_DISPATCH_MS`, `KV_HIT` to the trace?

alex: yes. will patch replay harness to optionally replay cache invalidation events (simulate new convo ids) and add the perf markers. Experiment plan: 3 runs each (streaming/replay, streaming/synth, non-streaming/replay) with `KERNEL_TRACE=1` and `MAX_BATCH_WAIT_MS` set to 25/10. Commands:
```
# replay (client timings + cache churn)
./tools/replay_harness --trace-file traces/session_042.rec --replay-client-timing --simulate-cache-churn --kernel-trace=1 --runs=3

# synth (uniform fire)
./tools/synth_driver --qps 1200 --chunk-size 256 --kernel-trace=1 --runs=3
```

tj: quick hypothesis to try before long runs: lower `max_batch_wait_ms` to 10ms and force `KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_fast` to reduce mixing slow kernels into batches. If that helps p99, then it's batching/backpressure combinatoric.

alex: ok will run both patches (lower wait + replay cache-churn) and post logs. If deploy-bot notices infra noise I'll pause.

deploy-bot: CI check: test-cluster available, reserved 8 gpus for 12m window :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — will update in this thread with results and raw kernel traces. :mag:
